topic: AI tool tutorial: a 5-minute privacy check-up for the apps you've connected to AI assistants
post:
When did you last check which apps your AI assistant can see? 🔐
Here's a 5-minute privacy check-up, inspired by Google's recent policy change.

Quick recap:
Google's updated privacy policy now lets Gmail, Drive and Photos data you connect to its AI features (Personal Intelligence) help shape ads. Connecting is opt-in, and Google says you can disconnect apps or change your Search data-sharing settings in your Google account.

The bigger lesson: every AI assistant you connect to your email, files or calendar deserves a regular check-up.

Your 5-minute check-up 👇
1️⃣ List every AI tool you've connected to your email, files or calendar
2️⃣ Open each tool's settings and find its connected apps or connectors
3️⃣ Disconnect anything you haven't used in the last month
4️⃣ Check whether your data can be used for ads or training, and turn it off if you can
5️⃣ Put a reminder in your calendar to repeat this every quarter 🗓️

Why it matters:
AI assistants get smarter with your data. That's the trade-off. You should decide what's worth sharing, not the default settings. ⚖️

Practical takeaway:
Do step 1 right now. Most people are surprised how long the list is. 📝
